note: Value-level oracle for the extracted cube engine. Recorded from the MONOLITH (cube/index.html), which is the same file main ships to the web, so a bundle compared against it is being compared against what the child actually plays. Re-record deliberately with `node cube/tools/cube-engine-sanity.mjs --record`.

CAPTION.R: right half rolls toward the ceiling
CAPTION.R': right half rolls toward the floor
CAPTION.L: left half rolls toward the floor
CAPTION.L': left half rolls toward the ceiling
CAPTION.U: ceiling row slides to your left
CAPTION.U': ceiling row slides to your right
CAPTION.D: floor row slides to your right
CAPTION.D': floor row slides to your left
CAPTION.F: facing side spins like clock hands
CAPTION.F': facing side spins the other way round
CAPTION.B: far side spins like clock hands
CAPTION.B': far side spins the other way round

righty.name: Righty chant
righty.say: Whole chants only, never stop halfway.
righty.what: Steps 1 and 2. It swaps your working corner with the block underneath.
righty.why: It only ever touches your working corner and the block underneath, so finished work is safe.

swap.name: Swap chant
swap.say: 14 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
swap.what: The step 3 one. It swaps the 2 blocks on your right, so the bar has to sit over on your left.
swap.why: It trades the two blocks on your right, which is why the bar hides on your left.

PRESETS.name: One turn away
PRESETS.hint: So close. One spin of the ceiling row finishes it.

quiz.q: How many sides show 2 matching squares nearest the ceiling?
quiz.why: All 4 sides match, so every block is already in its place. No chant. Just spin the ceiling row.

PRESETS.name: Two twists
PRESETS.hint: White floor is fine. Two ceiling blocks hide their yellow.
PRESETS.scramble: R' D' R D R' D' R D U R' D' R D R' D' R D R' D' R D R' D' R D U'

quiz.q: How many ceiling squares are yellow?
quiz.why: Two blocks still hide their yellow round the side. That is step 2 work. Righty chants, 2 or 4 each.

PRESETS.name: Headlights
PRESETS.hint: Yellow ceiling done. Two blocks want to trade places.
PRESETS.scramble: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'

quiz.q: How many sides show 2 matching squares?
quiz.why: Exactly one side matches. That side is the bar. Spin it over to your left, then Swap chant.

PRESETS.name: The Bar showdown
PRESETS.hint: Same idea, but you have to hunt for the bar first.
PRESETS.scramble: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' U2

quiz.q: Where does the bar go before the Swap chant?
quiz.why: The chant swaps the 2 blocks on your right, so the bar has to sit safely over on your left.

PRESETS.name: Criss-cross
PRESETS.hint: No bar anywhere. Chant once and one pops up.
PRESETS.scramble: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' U2 R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F' U2

quiz.q: How many sides show 2 matching squares?
quiz.why: None of them. So do the Swap chant once without turning the cube at all, and a bar appears.

PRESETS.name: Stripes
PRESETS.hint: A pattern, not a mess. The 4 sides go stripy.

quiz.q: Is white still all along the floor?
quiz.why: White stayed along the floor and yellow stayed at the ceiling. But every block is in the wrong place, so this one takes all three steps.

PRESETS.name: White layer only
PRESETS.hint: Step 1 is done for you. Start at step 2.
PRESETS.scramble: R U R' U R U2 R'

quiz.q: Which step do you start on?
quiz.why: The white layer is already built, so you go straight to getting yellow at the ceiling.

PRESETS.name: Full scramble
PRESETS.hint: The real thing. Three steps, two chants.
PRESETS.scramble: R U' F2 R' U R2 F' U2 R' F R'

quiz.q: What do you look for first?
quiz.why: Step 1 always starts by hunting a white square and holding it so it points at the ceiling.

words.CHANT_TWICE: Do it twice on a finished cube and the cube comes back finished. Every time. That is the drill.

cases.msg: Some squares are still empty. Colour all 24 in and I can help.

cases.how: square 3 painted a colour the cube does not have
cases.msg: One square is a colour I do not know.
Every colour needs exactly 4 squares. I count white: 5, yellow: 3. Have another look at your cube.

cases.how: corner slot 0 rotated on the spot

One block has two blue squares. Every block shows three different colours. Check the ringed one.

nodes.title: Just guide me
nodes.say: You do not have to tell me anything about your cube. I will call out every step and you do it on yours. The cube on this screen is only my example, so it will look different from yours. Do what I do, not what you see.
nodes.why: The three steps read the cube as you go, so they work on any mess without me knowing it.

nodes.title: Turn the whole cube over
nodes.say: Turn the cube round until you spot a white square, and hold it so that square points at the ceiling. That block is done.
nodes.why: Any white square will do to start, because that block is done the moment white points up.
nodes.src: Turn the cube round until you spot a white square, and hold it so that square points at the ceiling. That block is done.

ask.q: Have you got one white square pointing at the ceiling?

opts.label: My white layer is already done

nodes.title: Tip the whole cube toward you
nodes.say: Your white layer is already built. Hold the cube so white lies along the floor, and it stays there until the very end.
nodes.why: White goes to the floor now, so the messy step above can never touch it.
nodes.src: Your white layer is already built. Hold the cube so white lies along the floor, and it stays there until the very end.

nodes.title: White layer already built
nodes.say: Your white layer is already built and white is already along the floor. Straight on to step 2.
nodes.why: Your layer is already built, so there is nothing for this step to do.
nodes.src: Your white layer is already built and white is already along the floor. Straight on to step 2.

nodes.title: Find the next white block
nodes.say: Look for another white square, on a block you have not done yet. One of its other 2 colours has to touch the same colour on a done block. That is how you know where it goes.
nodes.why: Its other two colours must touch matching colours, and that is what says where it lives.
nodes.src: Look for another white square, on a block you have not done yet. One of its other 2 colours has to touch the same colour on a done block. That is how you know where it goes.

ask.q: Have you found a white square on a block you have not done yet?

nodes.title: Where is that block?
nodes.say: Look at where that block is sitting right now. Is it down in the floor row, or up at the ceiling in the wrong place?
nodes.why: A block already at the ceiling has to be popped down first, or there is nowhere for it to go.

ask.q: Where is that block?

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: This block is up at the ceiling, but not in its place. Spin the cube flat until it is at your working corner.
nodes.why: Spinning the whole cube flat moves nothing on it, so your done blocks stay done.
nodes.src: This block is up at the ceiling, but not in its place. Spin the cube flat until it is at your working corner.

nodes.title: Righty chant
nodes.say: One Righty chant. The block drops down to the floor row. Your done blocks stay safe.
nodes.why: Righty only swaps your working corner with the block underneath, so done blocks never move.
nodes.src: One Righty chant. The block drops down to the floor row. Your done blocks stay safe.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until the place this block belongs in is your working corner.
nodes.why: Spinning the whole cube flat moves nothing on it, so your done blocks stay done.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until the place this block belongs in is your working corner.

nodes.title: Turn only the floor row
nodes.say: Turn only the floor row until your block waits right below that place, like a lift.
nodes.why: Nothing in the floor row is finished yet, so you can spin it freely.
nodes.src: Turn only the floor row until your block waits right below that place, like a lift.

nodes.title: Righty chant
nodes.say: Righty chant. Your block dives down and pops back up. Keep going, whole chants only.
nodes.why: Each chant dives your block down and pops it back a new way round.
nodes.src: Righty chant. Your block dives down and pops back up. Keep going, whole chants only.

ask.q: Did it land in its place, with its white square at the ceiling?

nodes.title: Turn the whole cube over
nodes.say: All 4 white squares are at the ceiling. Turn the whole cube over. White lives at the floor now, and it stays there until the very end.
nodes.why: White goes to the floor now, so the messy step above can never touch it.
nodes.src: All 4 white squares are at the ceiling. Turn the whole cube over. White lives at the floor now, and it stays there until the very end.

nodes.title: Look before you chant
nodes.say: Before you do anything, look at the 4 squares up at the ceiling. Are they all yellow already?
nodes.why: All four ceiling squares are yellow already, so a chant here would only break it.

ask.q: Are all 4 ceiling squares yellow already?

nodes.title: Already all yellow
nodes.say: All 4 ceiling squares are yellow already. This step is done. Straight on to step 3.
nodes.why: All four ceiling squares are yellow already, so a chant here would only break it.
nodes.src: All 4 ceiling squares are yellow already. This step is done. Straight on to step 3.

nodes.title: Read this before you start
nodes.say: Halfway through this step your lovely white floor goes messy. That is not you breaking it. Finish every chant, keep white at the floor, and the white floor builds itself back the moment the last yellow square lands.
nodes.why: The mess is Righty keeping your white blocks safe. Six chants always puts them back.
nodes.src: Halfway through this step your lovely white floor goes messy. That is not you breaking it. Finish every chant, keep white at the floor, and the white floor builds itself back the moment the last yellow square lands.

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until a not yellow block arrives at your working corner.
nodes.why: A ceiling row spin never moves a floor block, so it cannot undo a chant you have done.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until a not yellow block arrives at your working corner.

nodes.title: Righty chant
nodes.say: Do the Righty chant 2 times. Then look at the working corner square.
nodes.why: The floor stays broken until the last yellow lands. Check the working corner square, not the floor.
nodes.src: That is 2 chants. Now look at the working corner square.
nodes.moves: R' D' R D R' D' R D

ask.q: Look at the working corner square. Is it yellow yet?

nodes.title: Count the ceiling
nodes.say: Look at all 4 ceiling squares. Are they all yellow now?
nodes.why: The floor stays broken until the last yellow lands, so count the yellow squares, not the floor.

ask.q: Are all 4 ceiling squares yellow?

nodes.title: Yellow ceiling done
nodes.say: All 4 ceiling squares are yellow, and look, the white floor came back exactly as it was.
nodes.why: The white floor put itself back together, because six Righty chants always land everything back home.
nodes.src: All 4 ceiling squares are yellow, and look, the white floor came back exactly as it was.

nodes.title: Read the four sides
nodes.say: Look at all 4 sides. On each side, look at the 2 squares nearest the ceiling. Do they match? It is always 0 sides, 1 side, or all 4. Never 2 or 3.
nodes.why: Two sides can never match on their own, so the count is only 0, 1 or 4.
nodes.src: Look at all 4 sides. On each side, look at the 2 squares nearest the ceiling. Do they match? It is always 0 sides, 1 side, or all 4. Never 2 or 3.

ask.q: How many sides show 2 the same?

nodes.title: Swap chant
nodes.say: No side matches at all. Do the Swap chant once without turning the cube. A bar will pop up.
nodes.why: With no bar, one chant makes one. Do it twice and you are back where you started.
nodes.src: No side matches at all. Do the Swap chant once without turning the cube. A bar will pop up.
nodes.moves: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'

nodes.title: Found the bar
nodes.say: Only one side matches, so that side is the bar.
nodes.why: The bar is the pair that already matches, so it has to stay out of the way.
nodes.src: Only one side matches, so that side is the bar. It is on your left.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat so the bar sits over on your left. The chant swaps the 2 blocks on your right, so the bar stays safely out of its way.
nodes.why: The chant swaps the two blocks on your right, so the bar hides on your left.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat so the bar sits over on your left. The chant swaps the 2 blocks on your right, so the bar stays safely out of its way.

nodes.title: Swap chant
nodes.say: Swap chant. 14 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
nodes.why: The Swap chant trades the two blocks on your right and leaves the bar alone.
nodes.src: Swap chant. 14 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
nodes.moves: R U R' U' R' F R2 U' R' U' R U R' F'

nodes.title: All 4 sides match
nodes.say: All 4 sides match, so every block is already in its place. No chant needed. One last spin and you are done.
nodes.why: All four match, so every block is home. A chant now would trade them away.
nodes.src: All 4 sides match, so every block is already in its place. No chant needed. One last spin and you are done.

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until every side is one colour.
nodes.why: Every block is home already, so one ceiling spin lines all the colours up.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until every side is one colour.

nodes.title: Look at your cube
nodes.say: Look at all four sides of your cube. Is every side one colour?
nodes.why: Three steps and two chants walked every block back to the place its colours named.

ask.q: Is every side one colour?

nodes.title: Solved
nodes.say: Every side is one colour. You solved it. Three steps, two chants.
nodes.why: Three steps and two chants walked every block back to the place its colours named.
nodes.src: Every side is one colour. You solved it. Three steps, two chants.

righty.name: Righty chant
righty.say: Whole chants only, never stop halfway.
righty.what: Steps 3 and 8. It swaps your working corner with the block underneath.
righty.why: It only ever touches your working corner and the block underneath, so finished work is safe.

rightdrop.name: Right-drop chant
rightdrop.say: 8 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
rightdrop.what: Step 4. It drops the block that is looking at you into the gap on your right.
rightdrop.why: It lifts the block out of the way, tucks it in, and puts the floor row back.

leftdrop.name: Left-drop chant
leftdrop.say: 8 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
leftdrop.what: Step 4. The mirror of Right-drop. It drops the block that is looking at you into the gap on your left.
leftdrop.why: The same trick the other way round, for the gap on your left.

crossmaker.name: Cross-maker chant
crossmaker.say: 6 moves. Say it out loud and never stop halfway.
crossmaker.what: Step 5. It turns a dot into an L, an L into a line, and a line into the yellow cross.
crossmaker.why: Held the way the picture says, it always moves you one picture closer to the cross.

edgespinner.name: Edge-spinner chant
edgespinner.say: 7 moves. Watch out for the double turn at the end.
edgespinner.what: Step 6. It shuffles three of the cross blocks round so their side squares find their middle squares.
edgespinner.why: It spins three of the four cross blocks round and leaves the fourth one standing.

cornermover.name: Corner-mover chant
cornermover.say: 8 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
cornermover.what: Step 7. It shuffles the other three corner blocks round and leaves your working corner alone.
cornermover.why: It shuffles the other three corners and leaves your working corner exactly where it is.

PRESETS.name: Daisy done
PRESETS.hint: Four white petals round the yellow middle square. Step 1 is done for you.
PRESETS.scramble: D F2 R B' R L' B' U B2 F' R2 F' U2 F' D U' F' R y U R

quiz.q: The daisy is made. Where does each petal go next?
quiz.why: One at a time, each petal lines up above the middle square of its own colour and then dives all the way down to the floor.

PRESETS.name: White cross done
PRESETS.hint: The cross is made and every arm matches its middle square. Corners next.

quiz.q: The white cross is facing the ceiling. What goes in next?
quiz.why: Step 3: the four white corner blocks, with the Righty chant you already know from the small cube.

PRESETS.name: One layer down
PRESETS.hint: The whole white layer is solid, white at the floor. Now the middle row.
PRESETS.scramble: U' B2 F' B' L U2 R' D' B' L R' D F' U D2 B2 y F' R y y U F' R D' F2 y y F2 yp F2 yp F2 yp F2 x2 yp D R' D' R D R' D' R D R' D' R D y y D2 R' D' R D R' D' R D R' D' R D x2

a: a block with no yellow square on it
quiz.why: Step 4 hunts along the ceiling row for 2 square blocks with no yellow on them. Those are the ones that live in the middle row.

PRESETS.name: Two layers done
PRESETS.hint: Only the yellow ceiling left to sort out.
PRESETS.scramble: U' F R U R' U' F'

quiz.q: Look at the four flat spots up at the ceiling. What can you see?
quiz.why: An L. Spin the cube flat until those two yellow blocks sit away from you and to your left, then do the Cross-maker chant.

PRESETS.name: Yellow cross made
PRESETS.hint: Yellow cross up top, but the side squares do not match yet.
PRESETS.scramble: R U R' U R U2 R' U R U' L' U R' U' L

quiz.q: Park the ceiling row at its best stop. How many of the four match?
quiz.why: Exactly 2. It is always all 4 or exactly 2, never 1 and never 3. Two matching means the Edge-spinner chant.

PRESETS.name: Corners to move
PRESETS.hint: The cross is matched all the way round. Now the corner blocks.
PRESETS.scramble: F R U R' U' R U R' U' R U R' U' F'

quiz.q: How many corner blocks are home?
quiz.why: None of them. So do the Corner-mover once from wherever you are holding the cube, and one block comes home.

PRESETS.name: The last twists
PRESETS.hint: Every corner is standing in its own place. Four of them are twisted.
PRESETS.scramble: F R U R' U' F' R U R' U R U2 R' F R U R' U' F' R U R' U R U2 R'

quiz.q: The corners are all in their own places. What is left to do?
quiz.why: Righty chants at the working corner, 2 or 4 each, and the cube does not spin again until the step is over.

PRESETS.name: Full scramble
PRESETS.hint: The real thing. Eight steps, six chants.
PRESETS.scramble: D F U2 F2 B2 L F2 D2 L2 U L F' U2 L2 F' U' D' B U R

quiz.q: A fresh mess. What do you make first?
quiz.why: The daisy: yellow middle square at the ceiling, with the four white 2 square blocks up beside it like petals.

nodes.title: Just guide me
nodes.say: You do not have to tell me anything about your cube. I will call out every step and you do it on yours. The cube on this screen is only my example, so it will look different from yours. Do what I do, not what you see.
nodes.why: The eight steps read the cube as you go, so they work on any mess without me knowing it.

nodes.title: Tip the whole cube toward you
nodes.say: Hold the cube so the yellow middle square points at the ceiling. Yellow is the colour on the far side from white.
nodes.why: Yellow at the ceiling means white is at the floor, which is where the cross belongs.
nodes.src: Hold the cube so the yellow middle square points at the ceiling. Yellow is the colour on the far side from white.

nodes.title: Find a white 2 square block
nodes.say: Hunt for a white 2 square block that is not a petal yet. We are bringing all four of them up beside the yellow middle square, like petals round a flower.
nodes.why: All four white blocks come up here first, so each one can dive straight down after.
nodes.src: Hunt for a white 2 square block that is not a petal yet. We are bringing all four of them up beside the yellow middle square, like petals round a flower.

ask.q: Have you found a white 2 square block that is not a petal yet?

nodes.title: Which row is it in?
nodes.say: Look at the white 2 square block you picked. Your cube has three rows: the ceiling row up beside the yellow middle square, the middle row round the waist, and the floor row at the bottom. Which row is your block sitting in?
nodes.why: Each row has its own way up to the daisy, so we take the one your block is really on.

ask.q: Which row is that block in?

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until that block is looking at you.
nodes.why: Yellow at the ceiling means white is at the floor, which is where the cross belongs.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until that block is looking at you.

nodes.title: Facing side spins like clock hands
nodes.say: Its white square is looking at you, not at the ceiling. Spin the facing side once and the block steps down into the middle row.
nodes.why: One turn tips it into the middle row, where the next turn can lift it properly.
nodes.src: Its white square is looking at you, not at the ceiling. Spin the facing side once and the block steps down into the middle row.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until that block sits between the side looking at you and your right.
nodes.why: Yellow at the ceiling means white is at the floor, which is where the cross belongs.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until that block sits between the side looking at you and your right.

nodes.title: Which way does it look?
nodes.say: Your block is in the middle row now, tucked between the side looking at you and your right. Look at its white square. Is it looking at you, or out to your right?
nodes.why: A white square looking at you rides up on the right half. One looking right swings up on the facing side. Same petal, different turn.

ask.q: Which way is its white square looking?

nodes.title: Which way does it point?
nodes.say: Your block is down in the floor row. Look at its white square. Is it pointing straight down at the floor, or out at one of the sides?
nodes.why: A white square already pointing down can go straight up in one turn. One pointing sideways has to step into the middle row first.

ask.q: Which way is its white square pointing?

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until an empty petal spot is looking at you.
nodes.why: The empty spot goes first, so the turn cannot knock off a petal you already made.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until an empty petal spot is looking at you.

nodes.title: Turn only the floor row
nodes.say: Spin only the floor row until your white block waits right underneath that empty spot.
nodes.why: No petals live in the floor row, so spinning it there costs you nothing.
nodes.src: Spin only the floor row until your white block waits right underneath that empty spot.

nodes.title: Facing side, twice
nodes.say: Turn the whole facing side twice. Your white block climbs all the way up and lands beside the yellow middle square. That is a petal.
nodes.why: A half turn carries it straight up with its white square still pointing at the ceiling.
nodes.src: Turn the whole facing side twice. Your white block climbs all the way up and lands beside the yellow middle square. That is a petal.

ask.q: Is that one up beside the yellow middle square now?

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until that block is down at the floor, looking at you.
nodes.why: Yellow at the ceiling means white is at the floor, which is where the cross belongs.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until that block is down at the floor, looking at you.

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row so there is no petal on the side looking at you.
nodes.why: The empty spot goes first, so the turn cannot knock off a petal you already made.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row so there is no petal on the side looking at you.

nodes.title: Facing side spins the other way round
nodes.say: Its white square is looking at you, so it cannot go straight up. Spin the facing side the other way round and it steps into the middle row.
nodes.why: Its white square looks at you, so it steps into the middle row first.
nodes.src: Its white square is looking at you, so it cannot go straight up. Spin the facing side the other way round and it steps into the middle row.

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until an empty petal spot is over on your right.
nodes.why: The empty spot goes first, so the turn cannot knock off a petal you already made.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until an empty petal spot is over on your right.

nodes.title: Right half rolls toward the ceiling
nodes.say: Roll the right half toward the ceiling. Your white block climbs up beside the yellow middle square. That is a petal.
nodes.why: Rolling the right half up carries its white square from looking at you to looking up.
nodes.src: Roll the right half toward the ceiling. Your white block climbs up beside the yellow middle square. That is a petal.

ask.q: Is that one up beside the yellow middle square now?

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until an empty petal spot is looking at you.
nodes.why: The empty spot goes first, so the turn cannot knock off a petal you already made.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until an empty petal spot is looking at you.

nodes.title: Facing side spins the other way round
nodes.say: Spin the facing side the other way round. Your white block climbs up beside the yellow middle square. That is a petal.
nodes.why: This turn swings a white square that was looking sideways round to point at the ceiling.
nodes.src: Spin the facing side the other way round. Your white block climbs up beside the yellow middle square. That is a petal.

ask.q: Is that one up beside the yellow middle square now?

nodes.title: The daisy
nodes.say: Yellow middle square at the ceiling, with four white petals round it. That is the daisy.
nodes.why: Four white blocks parked round yellow, each one above the colour it has to meet.
nodes.src: Yellow middle square at the ceiling, with four white petals round it. That is the daisy.

nodes.title: The daisy is already made
nodes.say: Your daisy is already made: yellow middle square at the ceiling with four white petals round it. Straight on to step 2.
nodes.why: Your daisy is already made, so this step has nothing left to do.
nodes.src: Your daisy is already made: yellow middle square at the ceiling with four white petals round it. Straight on to step 2.

nodes.title: The white cross is already made
nodes.say: Your white cross is already made and it is facing the ceiling. Straight on to step 3.
nodes.why: Your cross is already made, so this step has nothing left to do.
nodes.src: Your white cross is already made and it is facing the ceiling. Straight on to step 3.

nodes.title: Tip the whole cube toward you
nodes.say: Your whole white layer is already built. Hold the cube so white lies along the floor, and it stays there until the very end.
nodes.why: Spinning the whole cube flat moves nothing on it, so nothing you built moves.
nodes.src: Your whole white layer is already built. Hold the cube so white lies along the floor, and it stays there until the very end.

nodes.title: The white layer is already built
nodes.say: Your whole white layer is already built and white is already along the floor. Straight on to step 4.
nodes.why: Your whole white layer is already built, so we go straight on.
nodes.src: Your whole white layer is already built and white is already along the floor. Straight on to step 4.

nodes.title: The middle row is already done
nodes.say: The floor row and the middle row are both finished already. Straight on to step 5.
nodes.why: Both rows are already full, so there is nothing left to drop in.
nodes.src: The floor row and the middle row are both finished already. Straight on to step 5.

nodes.title: Pick a petal
nodes.say: Pick one petal and look at its side square, the one that is not white. That colour says where it has to go.
nodes.why: Its side square names the middle square it has to sit above before it dives.
nodes.src: Pick one petal and look at its side square, the one that is not white. That colour says where it has to go.

ask.q: Have you picked a petal that is still up at the ceiling?

opts.label: My white cross is already made

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your right
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until the red middle square is looking at you.
nodes.why: Spinning flat moves nothing on the cube, it only brings the work in front of you.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until the red middle square is looking at you.

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until that petal sits directly above the green middle square.
nodes.why: Only the ceiling row moves, so the petals stay petals and the floor is untouched.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until that petal sits directly above the green middle square.

nodes.title: Facing side, twice
nodes.say: Turn that whole side twice, a half turn. The petal dives all the way down to the floor.
nodes.why: A half turn drops the petal straight down onto its own colour on the floor.
nodes.src: Turn that whole side twice, a half turn. The petal dives all the way down to the floor.

nodes.title: Turn the whole cube over
nodes.say: Turn the whole cube over and look: a white cross facing the ceiling, and each arm's side square matching the middle square beside it. Leave the cube this way for step 3.
nodes.why: Turning over puts the cross at the ceiling, where the corner chant cannot disturb it.
nodes.src: Turn the whole cube over and look: a white cross facing the ceiling, and each arm's side square matching the middle square beside it. Leave the cube this way for step 3.

nodes.title: Find a white corner block
nodes.say: Find a white corner block that is not done yet. Its other 2 colours say where it belongs: the place up at the ceiling where the middle squares of those 2 colours meet.
nodes.why: Its other two colours name the two middle squares it has to sit between.
nodes.src: Find a white corner block that is not done yet. Its other 2 colours say where it belongs: the place up at the ceiling where the middle squares of those 2 colours meet.

ask.q: Have you found a white corner block that is not done yet?

opts.label: My white layer is already done

nodes.title: Where is that block?
nodes.say: Look at where that corner block is sitting right now. Is it down in the floor row, or up at the ceiling in the wrong place?
nodes.why: A block already at the ceiling has to be popped down first, or there is nowhere for it to go.

ask.q: Where is that block?

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: This block is up at the ceiling but not in its place yet. Spin the cube flat until it is at your working corner.
nodes.why: Spinning the whole cube flat moves nothing on it, so nothing you built moves.
nodes.src: This block is up at the ceiling but not in its place yet. Spin the cube flat until it is at your working corner.

nodes.title: Righty chant
nodes.say: One Righty chant. It drops down to the floor row. Your done blocks stay safe.
nodes.why: One chant drops the wrong block out, and your cross and finished corners stay put.
nodes.src: One Righty chant. It drops down to the floor row. Your done blocks stay safe.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your right
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until the place this block belongs in is your working corner.
nodes.why: Spinning the whole cube flat moves nothing on it, so nothing you built moves.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until the place this block belongs in is your working corner.

nodes.title: Turn only the floor row
nodes.say: Turn only the floor row until your block waits directly below that place, like a lift.
nodes.why: The floor row is unbuilt, so parking your block under its place is free.
nodes.src: Turn only the floor row until your block waits directly below that place, like a lift.

nodes.title: Righty chant
nodes.say: Righty chant. It lands in its place with its white square at the ceiling and its side colours touching the matching middle squares.
nodes.why: Each chant dives it down and pops it back a new way round, so 1, 3 or 5.
nodes.src: Righty chant. It lands in its place with its white square at the ceiling and its side colours touching the matching middle squares.

ask.q: Did it land in its place, with its white square at the ceiling?

nodes.title: Turn the whole cube over
nodes.say: All 4 white corner blocks are at the ceiling. Turn the whole cube over. White is at the floor now, and it stays there until the very end.
nodes.why: White lives at the floor from now on, underneath everything the next steps build.
nodes.src: All 4 white corner blocks are at the ceiling. Turn the whole cube over. White is at the floor now, and it stays there until the very end.

nodes.title: Hunt in the ceiling row
nodes.say: Look along the ceiling row for a 2 square block with no yellow square on it. Its side square is red, so it wants to be above the red middle square.
nodes.why: No yellow square means the block lives in the middle row, not up at the ceiling.
nodes.src: Look along the ceiling row for a 2 square block with no yellow square on it. Its side square is red, so it wants to be above the red middle square.

ask.q: What can you see in the ceiling row?

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until that block's side square sits directly above the middle square of the same colour.
nodes.why: Lining the side square over its own middle square is what makes the drop land right.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until that block's side square sits directly above the middle square of the same colour.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Now spin the cube flat until that block is looking at you. It makes an upside down T with the middle square under it.
nodes.why: Spinning flat brings the work in front of you without moving a single block.
nodes.src: Now spin the cube flat until that block is looking at you. It makes an upside down T with the middle square under it.

nodes.title: Right or left?
nodes.say: Look at that block's other square, the one pointing at the ceiling. It is blue. The blue middle square: is it to your right or to your left?
nodes.why: The ceiling square names the gap it belongs in, to your right or to your left.
nodes.src: Look at that block's other square, the one pointing at the ceiling. It is blue. The blue middle square: is it to your right or to your left?

ask.q: Is that middle square to your right or to your left?

nodes.title: Right-drop chant
nodes.say: To your right, so Right-drop. 8 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
nodes.why: The chant lifts the block over and tucks it into the gap, leaving the floor alone.
nodes.src: To your right, so Right-drop. 8 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
nodes.moves: U R U' R' U' F' U F

nodes.title: Left-drop chant
nodes.say: To your left, so Left-drop. 8 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
nodes.why: The chant lifts the block over and tucks it into the gap, leaving the floor alone.
nodes.src: To your left, so Left-drop. 8 moves, in 2 halves with a breath in the middle.
nodes.moves: U' L' U L U F U' F'

nodes.title: A stuck block
nodes.say: Every block left in the ceiling row has a yellow square on it, and a gap in the middle row is still holding the wrong block. You have to kick that block out first.
nodes.why: A wrong block is stuck in a gap, so something has to push it out first.
nodes.src: Every block left in the ceiling row has a yellow square on it, and a gap in the middle row is still holding the wrong block. You have to kick that block out first.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until the wrong gap is the one between the side looking at you and the side on your right.
nodes.why: Aim at the gap, not at the block, because the one going down is the wrong colour.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until the wrong gap is the one between the side looking at you and the side on your right.

nodes.title: Right-drop chant
nodes.say: Do the Right-drop chant once. Do not line anything up first: any block sitting in the ceiling row does this job, yellow or not. The stuck block pops up into the ceiling row where you can see it.
nodes.why: Any ceiling block can do the kicking. It just needs to land in the gap.
nodes.src: Do the Right-drop chant once. Do not line anything up first: any block sitting in the ceiling row does this job, yellow or not. The stuck block pops up into the ceiling row where you can see it.
nodes.moves: U R U' R' U' F' U F

nodes.title: Two layers
nodes.say: The floor row and the middle row are both finished. Only the yellow ceiling layer left.
nodes.why: Two whole layers done, and every chant from here leaves them exactly as they are.
nodes.src: The floor row and the middle row are both finished. Only the yellow ceiling layer left.

nodes.title: Look at the four flat spots
nodes.say: Look at the four flat spots up at the ceiling and ignore the corners. Which one of these is yours: a dot, an L, a line, or the cross?
nodes.why: There are only ever 0, 2 or 4 yellow flat spots, so those four pictures are everything.
nodes.src: Look at the four flat spots up at the ceiling and ignore the corners. Which one of these is yours: a dot, an L, a line, or the cross?

ask.q: Which one is yours?

nodes.title: Cross-maker chant
nodes.say: A dot. None of them is yellow, so do the chant from wherever you are holding the cube, then look again.
nodes.why: It turns a dot into an L, an L into a line, and a line into the cross.
nodes.src: A dot. None of them is yellow, so do the chant from wherever you are holding the cube, then look again.
nodes.moves: F R U R' U' F'

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your right
nodes.say: An L. Spin the cube flat until those two yellow blocks sit away from you and to your left.
nodes.why: Held the way the picture says, the chant moves you on. Held any other way you wander.
nodes.src: An L. Spin the cube flat until those two yellow blocks sit away from you and to your left.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: A line. Spin the cube flat until the line lies from your left to your right.
nodes.why: Held the way the picture says, the chant moves you on. Held any other way you wander.
nodes.src: A line. Spin the cube flat until the line lies from your left to your right.

nodes.title: Cross-maker chant
nodes.say: Now the Cross-maker chant. Then look again.
nodes.why: It turns a dot into an L, an L into a line, and a line into the cross.
nodes.src: Now the Cross-maker chant. Then look again.
nodes.moves: F R U R' U' F'

nodes.title: Already a cross
nodes.say: All four flat spots are yellow. That is the yellow cross. Nothing to do here, straight on to step 6.
nodes.why: The cross is already there, so a chant now would only take it apart again.
nodes.src: All four flat spots are yellow. That is the yellow cross. Nothing to do here, straight on to step 6.

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row and count, at each stop, how many of the four blocks have their side square the same colour as the middle square just below it. Leave it parked at the stop with the most.
nodes.why: Every stop gives a different count, so park where the most side squares match.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row and count, at each stop, how many of the four blocks have their side square the same colour as the middle square just below it. Leave it parked at the stop with the most.

nodes.title: How many match?
nodes.say: Count them. It is always all 4 or exactly 2. Never 1, never 3.
nodes.why: It is always all 4 or exactly 2, because a single swap cannot happen on a cube.
nodes.src: Count them. It is always all 4 or exactly 2. Never 1, never 3.

ask.q: How many of the four match?

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: The 2 that match are next to each other. Spin the cube flat until one of them is away from you and the other one is on your right.
nodes.why: The two that match sit away from you and on your right, or the chant loses them.
nodes.src: The 2 that match are next to each other. Spin the cube flat until one of them is away from you and the other one is on your right.

nodes.title: Edge-spinner chant
nodes.say: The 2 that match are opposite each other, so do the Edge-spinner once from wherever you are holding the cube. Then count again.
nodes.why: The chant spins three of the cross blocks round and leaves the fourth one standing.
nodes.src: The 2 that match are opposite each other, so do the Edge-spinner once from wherever you are holding the cube. Then count again.
nodes.moves: R U R' U R U2 R'

nodes.title: Edge-spinner chant
nodes.say: Now the Edge-spinner chant. Then count again.
nodes.why: The chant spins three of the cross blocks round and leaves the fourth one standing.
nodes.src: Now the Edge-spinner chant. Then count again.
nodes.moves: R U R' U R U2 R'

nodes.title: The cross is matched
nodes.say: Yellow cross at the ceiling and all four of its side squares matching the middle squares beside them. On to step 7.
nodes.why: The cross is matched the whole way round, so only the corner blocks are left.
nodes.src: Yellow cross at the ceiling and all four of its side squares matching the middle squares beside them. On to step 7.

nodes.title: How many are home?
nodes.say: A corner block is home when its 3 colours are the same 3 colours as the 3 middle squares around it. It is allowed to be twisted the wrong way round, that is fine here. Count all four before you chant.
nodes.why: Only none, 1 or all 4 can be home, because a plain two block swap cannot happen.
nodes.src: A corner block is home when its 3 colours are the same 3 colours as the 3 middle squares around it. It is allowed to be twisted the wrong way round, that is fine here. Count all four before you chant.

ask.q: How many corner blocks are home?

nodes.title: Corner-mover chant
nodes.say: None of them is home, so do the Corner-mover once from wherever you are holding the cube. One block comes home. Then count again.
nodes.why: The chant shuffles the other three round, so one more block finds its place.
nodes.src: None of them is home, so do the Corner-mover once from wherever you are holding the cube. One block comes home. Then count again.
nodes.moves: U R U' L' U R' U' L

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your left
nodes.say: Exactly 1 is home. Spin the cube flat until that one is at your working corner.
nodes.why: The chant leaves your working corner alone, so the finished block parks there and stays.
nodes.src: Exactly 1 is home. Spin the cube flat until that one is at your working corner.

nodes.title: Corner-mover chant
nodes.say: Now the Corner-mover chant. It shuffles the other three round and leaves your working corner alone. Then count again.
nodes.why: The chant shuffles the other three round, so one more block finds its place.
nodes.src: Now the Corner-mover chant. It shuffles the other three round and leaves your working corner alone. Then count again.
nodes.moves: U R U' L' U R' U' L

nodes.title: All four are home
nodes.say: All four are home already, so do not chant. Chanting now would throw three finished corners straight back out. On to step 8.
nodes.why: All four are already home, and a chant now would wreck them, so we skip it.
nodes.src: All four are home already, so do not chant. Chanting now would throw three finished corners straight back out. On to step 8.

nodes.title: Look before you chant
nodes.say: Before you do anything, look at the four corner squares up at the ceiling. Are they all yellow already?
nodes.why: Every corner square is yellow already, so chanting now would only twist them away.

ask.q: Are all four corner squares yellow already?

nodes.title: All four are already yellow
nodes.say: All four corner squares up at the ceiling are yellow already. No chanting needed. Straight to the last spin.
nodes.why: Every corner square is yellow already, so chanting now would only twist them away.
nodes.src: All four corner squares up at the ceiling are yellow already. No chanting needed. Straight to the last spin.

nodes.title: Read this before you start
nodes.say: Partway through this step your beautiful nearly finished cube goes messy. That is not you breaking it. Finish every chant, keep yellow at the ceiling, and the whole thing builds itself back the very moment the last yellow square lands at the ceiling.
nodes.why: The mess is Righty holding your layers safe. It all comes back on the last chant.
nodes.src: Partway through this step your beautiful nearly finished cube goes messy. That is not you breaking it. Finish every chant, keep yellow at the ceiling, and the whole thing builds itself back the very moment the last yellow square lands at the ceiling.

nodes.title: Spin the cube flat, to your right
nodes.say: Spin the cube flat until one of the blocks that is not yellow yet is at your working corner. That one flat spin, before your first chant, is safe. After it the cube does not spin again until the step is over.
nodes.why: Nothing is disturbed yet, so this one spin is free. After it, only the ceiling row.
nodes.src: Spin the cube flat until one of the blocks that is not yellow yet is at your working corner. That one flat spin, before your first chant, is safe. After it the cube does not spin again until the step is over.

nodes.title: Righty chant
nodes.say: Do the Righty chant 2 times. Then look at the block inside the red ring.
nodes.why: Yellow can only turn up after a whole pair, so look after two and never after one.
nodes.src: That is 2 chants. Now look at the working corner square. Is it yellow?
nodes.moves: R' D' R D R' D' R D

ask.q: Is its ceiling square yellow yet?

nodes.title: Count the corners
nodes.say: Look at the four corner squares up at the ceiling. Are they all yellow now?
nodes.why: Yellow can only turn up after a whole pair, so look after two and never after one.

ask.q: Are all four corner squares yellow?

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row to bring the next not yellow block to the working corner. Only the ceiling row from here.
nodes.why: Spinning the ceiling row keeps the mess where it is and brings the next block round.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row to bring the next not yellow block to the working corner. Only the ceiling row from here.

nodes.title: Spin only the ceiling row
nodes.say: Spin only the ceiling row until every side of the cube is one colour.
nodes.why: Everything is home, so one ceiling spin lines up all four sides at once.
nodes.src: Spin only the ceiling row until every side of the cube is one colour.

nodes.title: Look at your cube
nodes.say: Look at all six sides of your cube. Is every side one colour?
nodes.why: Eight steps and six chants walked every block back to the place its colours named.

ask.q: Is every side one colour?

nodes.title: Solved
nodes.say: Every side is one colour. You solved the big cube. Eight steps, six chants.
nodes.why: Eight steps and six chants walked every block back to the place its colours named.
nodes.src: Every side is one colour. You solved the big cube. Eight steps, six chants.
